bands.1:
"Stop them bots!" yells the Goldie.

He points at Wren. Rows of little gold robots turn round. Each one has one long finger.

How did you get here? Go back twenty minutes.

Twenty minutes ago, you have Madame Pause's badge. She is on your side.

"Maxx's lodge has a Comment Control Room, full stop," she says. "It deletes every question, full stop."

Indi's disguise is one giant snowman. The whole crew hides inside it.

"It has sixteen legs," says Tully.

"Snowmen come in all shapes," says Indi.

Two Goldies guard the lodge door. Gus opens a jar. Inside is a sock he wore for five weeks. The Goldies turn green and run.

Zed types GORGEOUSME. The door opens.

Inside, a big screen shows Maxx's stream. Rows of gold robots sit in front of it. A sign says, "DELETE ANY COMMENT WITH A QUESTION MARK."

"Is it scared?" Tap. Gone. "Is that a cage?" Tap. Gone.

A gold drive hums by the bots. It says, "DELETED QUESTIONS: 4,812,337."

"Proof," you whisper. You put it in your bag.

Wren creeps to the cages in the corner. Then the door bangs open. A Goldie runs in.

"Stop them bots!" he yells.

That brings you back to now. The bots stop. Then they start to switch each other off!

"He forgot the comma," you say. "Watch."

The last bot switches itself off.

"He meant, 'Stop them, comma, bots,'" says Madame Pause. "Instead, he told the bots to stop the bots, full stop."

Wren opens every cage. The Dotumbles roll out. The Throngle moths fly out in a cloud. The Goldie is covered in moths.

You all ride the chairlift down, laughing.

On the boat, Gus checks Maxx's stream. With no bots, the questions pile up. Then a new one pops up.

"Is that the Soggy Biscuit crew?"

A MaxxCam drone is right above the mast.

"Stay gold, Captain," says Maxx's voice. "You're live."
bands.2:
"Stop them bots!" bellows the Goldie, pointing straight at Wren.

All round the Comment Control Room, rows of gold Deletebots swivel to face her. Each one is the size of a toaster, with a single long finger. The crew is trapped between the bots and the door.

How did it come to this? Go back twenty minutes.

Twenty minutes earlier, Madame Pause's badge is pinned to your jacket, and she is on your side.

"Maxx's lodge has a Comment Control Room, full stop," she says, as Stoppit fluffs up on her ski pole. "Every question anyone asks Maxx, comma, it deletes, full stop."

Indi has made one enormous snowman costume. The whole crew fits inside it, plus Madame Pause.

"It has sixteen legs," says Tully.

"Snowmen come in all shapes," says Indi.

At the top of the chairlift, two Goldies guard the lodge door. The snowman shuffles past them. Behind their backs, Gus opens a jar holding one grey sock. "The Stink Sock," he whispers. "Five weeks of wearing it." The Goldies turn green and sprint down the mountain.

Zed types GORGEOUSME, and the inner door slides open.

Inside, one whole wall is a screen showing Maxx's live stream. In front of it sit the Deletebots. A sign says, "RULE ONE: DELETE ANY COMMENT WITH A QUESTION MARK."

"Is it scared?" Tap. Gone. "Is that a cage?" Tap. Gone.

Behind the bots, a gold hard drive hums. Its label says, "DELETED QUESTIONS. DO NOT LOOK. 4,812,337 AND COUNTING."

"Proof," you whisper, and slide it into your bag.

Wren creeps towards the glass cages in the corner. Then the door bangs open, and a Goldie bursts in with streaming eyes.

"Stop them bots!"

And that brings you back to now. Every bot freezes. Then, one by one, they reach out their long fingers and switch each other off.

"He forgot the comma," you say. "Watch."

Click, click, click. The last Deletebot switches itself off.

"He meant, 'Stop them, comma, bots,'" says Madame Pause happily. "Instead, comma, he told the bots to stop the bots, full stop."

Wren flings open the cages. Dotumbles roll out like marbles, and the Throngles pour out in a cloud of moths. The Goldie vanishes under them.

You ride the creaking chairlift down the mountain, laughing all the way.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, Gus opens Maxx's stream. With no bots left, the questions are piling up. Then a new one appears at the top.

"Is that the Soggy Biscuit crew on the chairlift?"

Slowly, you look up. A MaxxCam drone is hovering above the mast.

"Stay gold, Captain," says Maxx's voice. "You're live."
bands.3:
"Stop them bots!" bellows the Goldie, pointing straight at Wren.

All round the Comment Control Room, rows of gold Deletebots swivel to face her. Each one is the size of a toaster, with a single long finger, and every finger is pointing her way. Wren's hand is on a cage door. The rest of the crew is frozen between the bots and the only exit.

How did the heist come to this? Go back twenty minutes.

Twenty minutes earlier, Madame Pause's badge is pinned to your jacket, and you are riding her private chairlift, an old wooden one that creaks like a haunted rocking chair.

"The gold lodge has one door, comma, two guards and no sense of humour, full stop," she says. "Inside is the Comment Control Room, full stop. Every question anyone asks Maxx, comma, it deletes, full stop."

Stoppit, her round red robin, fluffs up on her ski pole as if to agree.

Indi has built one enormous snowman costume out of three bedsheets, a mop bucket and a carrot. The whole crew is supposed to fit inside it, plus Madame Pause.

"It has sixteen legs," says Tully.

"Snowmen come in all shapes," says Indi.

At the top of the chairlift, two Goldies guard the lodge. The snowman shuffles towards them. Its carrot falls off, and Mo sticks it back on upside down.

"Nice snowman," says one Goldie.

"Thanks," says the snowman, in eight voices.

Then Gus unscrews a jar holding one grey ski sock, worn every day for five weeks. The smell rolls out like fog. Both Goldies turn green and sprint down the mountain with their hands over their noses.

Zed tries MAXXISGREAT on the inner door. Wrong. He tries GORGEOUSME, and the door slides open.

One whole wall of the Comment Control Room is a screen showing Maxx's stream, with comments pouring up the side. In front of it sit the Deletebots, under a sign: "RULE ONE: DELETE ANY COMMENT WITH A QUESTION MARK."

"Is it scared?" Tap. Gone. "Why is it shaking?" Tap. Gone. "Is that a cage?" Tap. Gone.

Behind the bots hums a gold hard drive: "DELETED QUESTIONS. DO NOT LOOK. 4,812,337 AND COUNTING."

"Proof," you whisper, and slide it into your bag.

In the corner, glass cages are stacked to the ceiling, full of Dotumbles, Stashlets and a jar of Throngle moths. Wren creeps towards them. She has just reached the first lock when the door bangs open, and one of the Goldies bursts back in, his eyes still streaming.

"Stop them bots!"

Which brings you back to now. Every bot freezes. Then, one by one, they reach out their long fingers and switch each other off.

Madame Pause looks puzzled. You start to grin.

"He forgot the comma," you say. "Watch."

Click, click, click, click. The last Deletebot switches itself off.

"He meant, 'Stop them, comma, bots,'" says Madame Pause, delighted. "Instead, comma, he told the bots to stop the bots, full stop. Tragic, full stop."

Wren flings open the cages. Dotumbles roll out like marbles, Stashlets scurry for the door, and the Throngles pour out in a fluttering cloud. The Goldie disappears under a blizzard of moths.

You ride the creaking chairlift down the mountain with the Creatures in your arms, laughing so hard the chair wobbles.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, Gus opens Maxx's stream. With no bots left, the questions are piling up, thousands of them. Then a brand-new one appears at the top.

"Is that the Soggy Biscuit crew on the chairlift?"

Slowly, you look up. A MaxxCam drone is hovering above the mast, its red light blinking.

"Stay gold, Captain," says Maxx's voice. "You're live."
bands.4:
"Stop them bots!" bellows the Goldie, one shaking finger aimed at Wren.

All round the Comment Control Room, rows of gold Deletebots swivel to face her, each the size of a toaster, each with a single long finger, and every finger now pointing the same way. Wren's hand is on a cage door. The rest of the crew is wedged between the bots and the only exit, and nobody, for once, has a plan.

To understand how a perfectly good heist ends up here, go back twenty minutes.

Twenty minutes earlier, Madame Pause's badge is pinned to your jacket, and you are swaying up the mountain on her private chairlift, an old wooden thing that creaks like a haunted rocking chair.

"The gold lodge has one door, comma, two guards and no sense of humour, full stop," she says, while Stoppit fluffs up on her ski pole. "Inside is the Comment Control Room, full stop. Every question anyone asks Maxx, comma, it deletes, full stop."

Indi has been up all night. What she unveils, after a long and painful silence, is a single enormous snowman made of three bedsheets, a mop bucket and a carrot, built to hold the entire crew and one tall ski instructor.

"Nobody looks twice at a snowman," says Indi. "It's a snowy island."

"It has sixteen legs," says Tully.

"Snowmen come in all shapes."

At the top of the lift, two Goldies in gold earmuffs guard the lodge door. The snowman shuffles towards them, and its carrot drops into the snow. Mo picks it up and puts it back on upside down.

"Nice snowman," says one Goldie.

"Thanks," says the snowman, in eight voices.

Behind their backs, Gus unscrews a jar holding one grey ski sock, worn every day for five weeks, through two footy matches and a swamp. The smell rolls out like a fog bank. Both Goldies turn green, then grey, then sprint down the mountain with their hands clamped over their noses.

At the inner door, Zed starts thinking aloud. "Okay so he's used MAXXISGREAT and ILOVEME and he thinks those are clever so maybe he's added..."

Stoppit pecks him on the ear. Zed, who has just been taught something about sentences that never end, types GORGEOUSME, and the door slides open.

The Comment Control Room is the size of a basketball court. One whole wall is a screen showing Maxx's live stream, and up its side pours a waterfall of comments. In front of it, row after row, sit the Deletebots, under a sign that reads "RULE ONE: DELETE ANY COMMENT WITH A QUESTION MARK."

"Is it scared?" Tap. Gone. "Why is it shaking?" Tap. Gone. "Is that a cage?" Tap. Gone.

Not one of the deleted comments is rude. Every one of them is worried.

Behind the bots, humming hotter than anything else in the room, sits a gold hard drive: "DELETED QUESTIONS. DO NOT LOOK. 4,812,337 AND COUNTING."

"Proof," you whisper, sliding it into your bag.

In the corner, glass cages are stacked to the ceiling: Dotumbles asleep in tight balls, Stashlets with their noses to the glass, a jar so full of Throngle moths that it seems to breathe. Wren goes to them without being asked. She has her fingers on the first lock when the door bangs open behind you, and one of the Goldies bursts back in, his eyes still streaming from the sock.

"Stop them bots!"

Which brings you back to now: Wren, the bots, the fingers, the door.

Every bot freezes. Then, one by one, they reach out their long fingers, not towards Wren, but towards each other, and begin to switch each other off.

Madame Pause looks puzzled. You, however, have spent a whole island learning what one small mark can do, and you start to grin.

"He forgot the comma," you say. "Watch."

Click, click, click, click, down the rows, until the last Deletebot, finding nobody left to stop, carefully switches itself off.

"He meant, 'Stop them, comma, bots,'" says Madame Pause, delighted. "Instead, comma, he told the bots to stop the bots, full stop. Tragic, full stop."

Wren flings the cages open. Dotumbles roll out like dropped marbles, Stashlets scurry for the door, and the Throngles pour from their jar in a cloud so thick that the Goldie simply vanishes inside it, still pointing.

You sway back down the mountain on the creaking chairlift, Creatures in your arms, laughing so hard the whole chair wobbles.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, Gus opens Maxx's stream on the cracked tablet. With no bots left to delete them, the questions are piling up, thousands of them, from every corner of the world. Then a new one appears at the top, posted three seconds ago.

"Is that the Soggy Biscuit crew on the chairlift?"

Nobody moves. Slowly, you look up. Hovering above the mast, its red light blinking, is a MaxxCam drone.

"Stay gold, Captain," says Maxx's voice. "You're live."
